target_customer: Biodefense and public health buyers for diagnostics; later biopharma scientists for the Amina protein engineering agent.
problem: Point-of-care diagnostics for emerging biological threats take over a year to develop; the company aims to design them in days with AI.
business_model: Diagnostics development for biodefense buyers, later a software platform for protein engineering; pricing not found
product_category: Biotech and AI protein engineering, biodefense diagnostics

founders.name: Abhi Rajendran
founders.background_notes: YC page: ex-Mercedes Formula 1 engineer and computational biologist. Education not on the YC page.

founders.name: Adam Wu
founders.background_notes: Company site says formerly of Procter & Gamble; YC page says he is building the smartest protein engineer in the world.

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing protein-based sensors with language models and validating them as working diagnostics needs wet lab validation and regulatory work as well as ML.

defensibility.rationale: Validated sensor designs and academic links (an Imperial College chief scientist is named on the company site) are hard to copy, but protein design tools were open and spreading.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found. Search results showed only older academic and defense efforts in biothreat diagnostics, not a funded startup rival.

market_need_then: Biodefense diagnostics have government demand, with defense funding programs appearing in search results, but no direct demand evidence for this company was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses aminoanalytica.com, the exact name plus .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission framing: Protecting Civilization from Biological Threats

branding.brand_signature: Amina, the name of the AI protein engineering agent
branding.community_and_virality: A public CLI package and a skills collection let Claude Code use the Amina tools, per search results.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive science name that is long and easy to misspell; the sub-brand Amina is shorter, and its use in developer tooling shows some pull, but little press.

pivots.to: Amina, an AI agent for protein engineering
pivots.why: Not stated; a second YC launch reframed the company as an agent platform per a search summary, but the date is unknown. The YC tagline and company site still carry the biodefense message.

outcome_analysis: The company is active in London with three people. It positions around AI-designed diagnostics and has launched Amina, an agent for protein engineering, which suggests a broadening toward a software product. No funding or traction was publicly verified, so the outcome cannot be judged.
notes: Dealroom shows a garbled funding table (about 10K GBP seed and about 125K USD seed) and another aggregator shows $750K revenue; both unverified, no round recorded. The ARIA logo on the company site is a partner mention only; an unrelated Aria Diagnostics appears in search. An Imperial College blog (not opened) was said to describe Rajendran as an undergraduate there, so education is left empty. No dated competitor sources near the batch were found. Completeness pass: the 500K seed rests on aggregators only (Extruct, with date given as 2025 by one and July 2024 by another, so date left null; Caplight shows a total of 1.01M); no press or filing confirms it, so history is partial.
